Solve the lexicographic program

Source: R/solve_lexicographic.R
solve_lexicographic.Rd

Solves the preemptive goal program level by level (Rocha, 2026, section 4.4.1): level l minimizes the weighted sum of the penalized deviations of its goals, with the levels already solved locked at their optima (d_j == Z_j, j < l). Works for any number of levels and any number of goals per level.

Usage

solve_lexicographic(lp, priorities, keep_lp = FALSE, lock_tolerance = 0)

Arguments

lp

Object of class lexio_lp from build_lp().

priorities

List of levels, in priority order. Each level is a list with name and either terms (a list of goals, each with rows of G, type ("minus", "plus" or "both", see direction_type()) and weight) or, for a level with a single goal of weight 1, rows and type.

keep_lp

If TRUE, keeps the ROI OP object of each level.

lock_tolerance

0 (default): exact lock d_l == Z_l. t > 0: relaxed lock d_l <= Z_l + t * max(1, |Z_l|) (see lock_tolerance in define_model()).

Value

List with levels (one element per level: GLPK status, objval, x, d_plus, d_minus, gx = G x and violation, the largest violation of the constraints of the level by that solution, see run_experiment()), Z (the optima of the levels), checks (data frame) and lock_tolerance.

Details

Each LP is solved with ROI::ROI_solve(op, solver = "glpk") and the default solver options. After each run two checks are applied: the optimum of each level equals the sum of its penalized deviations, and every earlier level stays at its optimum.
